accuracy.evidence: Every scored sentence checked against standard agreement rules: head noun governs the verb past prepositional and 'as well as' phrases (the box of crayons is, my shoes as well as my coat are), one of/each/every/everyone singular, compound subjects with and plural, proximity rule for either … or and neither … nor, subject after the verb in there is/are, pronouns matching antecedent number across sentences (the bikes … them). Collective nouns and singular they are deliberately left out of scored items because British English and current style guides accept both forms; the adult text says so instead of marking them wrong.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented agreement slips: attraction to the nearest noun (the key to the doors are, one of my friends have), there is with a plural subject, each treated as plural, the wrong subject chosen under neither … nor, a plural pronoun for a singular antecedent hidden behind 'of pens', and it for a plural antecedent in the previous sentence. Each has its own miss message in the lab and a challenge tag (near, there, nor, each, ante, pnear, and).

lab_distinct.evidence: The mechanism is subject-finding: tapping the head noun visibly strikes out the modifying phrase and fills the verb, verb tiles are dragged into a gap, and the pronoun step draws a link from the gap back to its antecedent, including across a sentence boundary. flagsva (basic he runs / they run) and flagagree (resolving disagreements, a Personal & Social lab) do neither; lab_distinct gate under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners find the rule by doing: the first task makes them tap the head noun before any verb is shown, and the crossed-out phrase reveals why 'is' fits. Wrong drags quote the real subject (Cross out “of apples”: the bag is heavy). The note task then asks them to transfer all three ideas to unfamiliar sentences without a gap to guide them.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions, each with the attraction-style wrong answer as the tempting option: 'The box of crayons are', 'One of my friends have', 'Neither the cat nor the dogs is', 'The box of pens fell. Their lid'. The following task disproves each and A.reveal reports the result.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Eight rotating questions with eleven tagged wrong answers, each with a correction naming the slip, e.g. 'That verb matches the noun just before the gap. Cross out the phrase and match the head noun' and 'Find the antecedent in the sentence before: the dogs, more than one, so them.'

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and define subject, head noun and antecedent before using them, each with a concrete sentence; terms are the curriculum's own (subject, verb, singular, plural, pronoun, antecedent). The validator's readability limits (kid ≤ 6.5, adult ≤ 9.5) pass.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph teaches one rule with an example; the adult text gives the standard, the rules, the five lab tasks and the named mistakes. The content gate's filler and 12% similarity checks pass, including against 415 Subject-verb agreement.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px Android-size screenshots of every step: word tiles wrap and centre with no clipping, verb and pronoun tiles are 54 px tall and 110 px wide, the antecedent link and label sit clear of the tiles, and every canvas action also has a full-size button below the lab.

accessibility.evidence: Buttons for every action (each word of the sentence, both verbs, both pronouns, each checkable word in the note); the canvas aria-label reads the feedback and the current sentence with 'blank' for the gap; walk.cjs found no axe WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark theme on desktop and iPhone 13, with no console errors.
